Video Thumbnail

A video's thumbnail as one control: the whole picture is the button, with a pink play disc centred on it. You bring the picture and the size; it brings the edge, the disc and the hover.

Slot-basedAny sizeToken-driven

Preview

Hover it, or tab to it: the edge goes white, the picture leans in to 1.03 and the disc to 1.1. The scales stop under prefers-reduced-motion.

Sizes

The box is the page’s: give it a width and an aspect-* through class, so the picture is never re-cropped by the viewport. playSize sets the disc as a percentage of the box’s inner width, so it scales with the box; the default, 16.22, is Why IronPDF’s 64px disc on a 395px card.
476 × 270 · playSize 12.4497the homepage hero
248 × 140 · playSize 19.592the Iron Suite hero

Token Reference

Code

          
<VideoThumbnail
  label="Play the video: What is Iron Suite?"
  playSize={12.4497}

  <img src={thumbnail} alt="" />
</VideoThumbnail>

Guidelines

✓ Do
  • Give the box an aspect-*, not a fixed height: a fixed height under a fluid width re-crops the picture at every other width.
  • Name the video in label — “Play the video: What is Iron Suite?”. The picture is decoration.
  • Fill the slot edge to edge: absolute inset-0 size-full object-cover on the image.
✗ Don't
  • Don't put another control inside it — the whole picture is already the button.
  • Don't size the disc in pixels; a fixed disc sits differently on every width the box takes.
  • Don't use it on a light surface without checking the edge — it is drawn for a dark one.
